subject: Reallocation of Indemnity Defense / Order Form - request for approval
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@heliomed.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: mike.olson@venturelaw.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redline - defense control / order form indemnity

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the MSA + order form and we circulated a redline focused on Section 9 (Indemnification). Two items we can't accept as drafted:

- "Right to defend" language that gives Redwood sole control for third-party IP claims tied to model outputs. Given HelioMed's regulatory risk, we need the right to lead defense for claims tied to clinical decision-support outputs.
- The proposed cap and subrogation carve create gaps for us on third-party claims that allege customer data causation.

I've attached HelioMed_MSA_redline_v3.docx with inline comments. Our suggested compromise is a bifurcated approach: HelioMed may assume defense control for claims that are demonstrably caused by outputs that the customer directly relied on in clinical workflows; Redwood retains defense when the claim alleges core model training data or open-source infringement. We also suggest a 30-day evidence-handback SLA and an explicit insurer-notice coordination clause.

Can we set a 30-minute call next week to align counsel? If helpful, Mike Olson (cc'd) is HelioMed's outside counsel and will lead the redline walk-through.

Best,

Sara Lin
General Counsel
HelioMed, Inc.

Attachment: HelioMed_MSA_redline_v3.docx (Microsoft Word, 48KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@heliomed.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, mike.olson@venturelaw.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redline - defense control / order form indemnity

Sara —

Thanks for the clear note and the redline. We appreciate HelioMed surfacing the clinical-risk angle. High level thoughts:

- We can accept a "lead defense" carve for customer-adopted clinical outputs, but we need objective triggers and a mutual handback path. Suggested trigger: a reproducible test or evidence (logs/prompt set + timestamped usage) showing the output was consumed in a regulated workflow.
- For third-party IP claims alleging model-training-data infringement, Redwood must retain defense; that's where we have the records and control.
- 30-day evidence-handback SLA is reasonable; we prefer an incremental step: 14 days to review evidence, then 30 days to transfer custody with escrow details.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick call Tuesday 10/5 at 10am PT to walk the redline (30 minutes).
2) If we agree on triggers, we'll produce a short addendum to the Order Form specifying evidence required and the evidence-preservation timeline.
3) Legal to exchange insurer contact details and confirm subrogation carve language.

I've looped Kim (GC) for legal signoff and Ben (Sales lead / deal owner) for procurement acceptance.

Thanks — happy to take the call.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Legal Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm-HLMD-0421.pdf (Order Form draft)

Subject: Fwd: Initial redline - defense control / order form indemnity (internal notes)

Kim / Ben —

Forwarding HelioMed's redline. Quick internal take before Tue call:

- Risk profile: HelioMed is high because the output affects clinical decisions. We can concede "lead defense" for customer-adopted outputs only if the trigger is narrowly defined and we keep operational control of discovery for training-data claims.
- Ops burden: evidence preservation + escrow staging will require a short playbook (ops ticket, SRE snapshot window, and a legal handoff checklist). That adds ~2 engineering hours per incident + 1 legal hour. We should include an SLA credit collar in finance if this becomes frequent.
- Commercial: ask for an incremental indemnity fee (modest uplift) or a per-claim cap that scales with ARR to protect Redwood's unit economics. Ben — can you flag whether HelioMed will accept a small uplift in the order form?

Planned to propose at the call: 14-day initial review, 30-day physical handback with escrow; specific evidence list (prompt ID, model version, user session ID, timestamped consumer receipt). If HelioMed pushes back, propose a neutral third-party arbiter for trigger disputes.

Olga
Head of Legal Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Olga / Sara / team —

Thanks for the call this morning — that cleared a lot up. HelioMed is comfortable moving forward with the bifurcated approach subject to the following eds:

- Trigger language: replace subjective wording with an objective list. We agreed on: (i) model version identifier, (ii) unique prompt/session ID that maps to a recorded clinical workflow step, and (iii) evidence of documented adoption (signed SOP or deployment ticket).
- Evidence-handback window: HelioMed accepts 14-day review + 30-day transfer; request Redwood provide an ops contact and an SRE snapshot manifest within 48 hours of notice.
- Commercial: HelioMed will accept a limited uplift to the order form price (1.5% of annual subscription for indemnity services) in exchange for HelioMed leading defense in narrow cases.

I've prepared a short order-form addendum and a DocuSign envelope. If Redwood confirms acceptance, we'll finalize the addendum and route for signatures.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/HLMD/Envelope/123abc

Mike Olson
